summary.headline: Bajaj Auto Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR16,006 crores with EBITDA of INR3,323 crores at 20.8%, but management flags April-onward commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 set records for revenue, EBITDA and volumes, with 2W, 3W and exports each growing about 20% in volume and 30% in revenue. Margins held at 20.8% helped by a stronger rupee (realised INR90.6/USD vs INR86.5 a year ago), richer mix and operating leverage, offsetting net commodity inflation of about 40 bps and absorbed PM E-DRIVE subsidy loss on electric 3-wheelers. Management guided to a sharply weaker operating backdrop from April: domestic motorcycle growth seen at 7-9% near term versus about 20% in Q4, plus 10-15% supply loss, and commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue, about 40% of which has been priced in so far. The board also approved a 100% payout of FY26 profit (dividend INR150/share plus a INR5,633 crore buyback at INR12,000/share).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Crossed 6 lakh units for second straight quarter, +25% YoY, highest-ever quarterly export revenue; FY26 revenue USD2.2 billion (record). KTM exports from India ~17,500 units in Q4 vs near nil a year ago; Nigeria back above 1 lakh units in Q4 but FY26 flat vs FY25.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles (2W)
segments.commentary: Industry grew ~11% in FY26 and ~20% in Q4. Bajaj 150cc+ share recovering; 10 Pulsar variants/upgrades launched Oct-Mar now 50% of sales. Q4 KTM+Triumph domestic volumes ~43,000 units, +43% YoY (record).

segments.name: Electric (2W + 3W)
segments.commentary: Now ~20%+ of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin for last two quarters; Chetak EBITDA-neutral. Chetak Q4 retails above 1 lakh (record), March above 50,000; share ~23%, up 170 bps QoQ. FY26 Chetak revenue INR4,000 crores, over 5 lakh units.

segments.name: 3-wheelers
segments.commentary: Electric 3W No.1 in registrations through Q4 and April; industry 3W growth 25%+ in Q4 and April. Commercial vehicles crossed 5 lakh units in FY26; Q4 volumes +28% YoY; CNG share close to 90%.

segments.name: Spares
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,700+ crores, +16% growth, record EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL)
segments.commentary: AUM nearly INR19,000 crores (roughly doubled); FY26 PAT INR665 crores vs INR58 crores; CRAR 19.5%; ROE ~23%; 1.8 million customers.

guidance_outlook: Domestic motorcycle industry growth estimated at 7-9% in the near term (based on April outcomes), versus about 20% in Q4; growth expected mainly from 125cc+ and 150cc+ segments, which management expects to grow about twice the industry rate.
Exports targeted at 2.2 lakh units per month in Q1 FY27 (from 2.0 lakh), with Gulf loss of about 5,000-6,000 units per month.
Material commodity cost inflation of about 3.5-4% of revenue (Q1 vs Q4); about 40% offset by pricing so far; management says the next price action may be the last, if needed.
Supply constraints (LPG, manpower, logistics) impaired April serviceability by 10-15%; expected to ease over time.

Buyback of INR5,633 crores at INR12,000/share needs shareholder approval; process expected to conclude by end-July with payout around second week of July; final dividend INR150/share (INR4,192 crores) after July AGM.
KTM turnaround results expected to show up in the latter part of 2026. KTM and BMAG to move to quarterly reporting with one-quarter lag.
New Pulsar 125cc and 150cc+ launches targeted from July.
capex_capacity: Chetak capacity now 50,000 units per month; management expects to max it out and says a substantive capacity increase is needed, with plan to be announced later.
Brazil plant capacity ~60,000 units per annum (about 50,000 usable), expected to be fully used within 12 months; further expansion considered by mid-year for FY27-28.
FY26 capex about INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV; over INR2,300 crores invested in BACL and BAIH BV.
Larger 3-wheeler capacity (7 and 9 series) is becoming a constraint; expansion underway.
demand_pricing: Price hikes effective 1 April across products; management says 30-40% of the GST-cut benefit could be rolled back, weighing on demand.
Realisation of USD/INR around 94-95 currently vs INR90.6 average in Q4; company is unhedged and realises at market.
Commodity moves: noble metals up 35-45%, aluminium up 35-45%, copper ~20%, steel ~15% in the current quarter.
Nigeria fuel prices up about 30%; Nigeria running at 35,000+ units per month for motorcycles plus 5,000+ 3W.
Brazil at 5th position in share in April; Latam 11 consecutive quarters of growth; Mexico and FTA outlook cited as upside.
Competitive pressure: management says 125cc bikes from China are a competitive threat in export markets.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price hike affected demand, and are exports seeing similar effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said motorcycle industry growth fell from Q4 to April and that 30-40% of the GST benefit may roll back. Upper-half and 150cc+ demand remains strong, while Latam and Nigeria are healthy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company hedged on currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dinesh Thapar said the company is not hedged and realises at market rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports outgrow domestic volumes in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast the split but said exports are on a strong footing, targeting above 2 lakh units per month in Q1, and that the 150cc+ domestic segment is also performing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to lift Chetak beyond the ~30,000/month run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 50,000 units per month and management expects to max it; a larger capacity expansion is under study and will be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 125cc affordable motorcycle launch this year, and what is the PLI amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name a model but said new 125cc and 150cc+ Pulsar launches are coming from July. CFO said PLI for FY26 is about INR900 crores, still being aggregated.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from the 3.5-4% commodity inflation, and what is the margin tolerance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is to hold margins at steady state, that the estimate has been refreshed three times in four weeks, and that pricing may be the last lever, with cost savings and discretionary spend cuts used first. Currency at INR94-95 is a partial cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-9% industry outlook for the next few months or the full year, and is 3-wheeler growth structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7-9% covers the next few months, not the full year, with a base effect in H2. It said 3W industry growth is 25%+ and structural, driven by non-metro mobility, shared ticketing and larger 3W formats.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving other operating income, and what are the milestones for the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Other operating income is driven by PLI on electric scale-up, export incentives and BGO oils royalty. Buyback needs shareholder approval because it exceeds 10% of free reserves (about INR3,500 crores); process expected to finish by end-July, with payout around the second week of July.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 3.5-4% of revenue in Q1 and possibly more; pricing may be exhausted after the next round; figures are reviewed monthly.
Domestic motorcycle growth could slow to 7-9% as GST benefit rolls back, with a base effect in H2.
Supply constraints of 10-15% (LPG, manpower, logistics) and Middle East disruption (Gulf loss about 5,000-6,000 units per month).
KTM turnaround still in progress; KTM and BMAG results consolidated with a one-quarter lag and the accounting includes non-recurring gains and FCTR reclassification.
Nigeria fuel price increase of about 30% could affect demand; competitive pressure from Chinese 125cc bikes in export markets.
Buyback of INR5,633 crores needs shareholder approval; cash-flow and approval timing to monitor.
Management's rupee tailwind (INR94-95) is unhedged and could reverse.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the export and EV franchises, but noticeably cautious on the near-term outlook: management repeatedly called the cost environment "very dynamic" and "month by month" and gave no full-year guidance. Some answers on pricing tolerance and margin outcome were non-committal.
